Starting from the United States Grand Prix weekend on Friday, October 23, Apple TV will provide Formula 1 live broadcasts in Dolby Atmos format on supported devices, with details as follows.

"Combining top-tier visuals and sound to fully present the passion and energy of this sport"

Apple and Dolby Laboratories have announced a new partnership, bringing Dolby Atmos technology to Formula 1 live broadcasts on Apple TV, with the racing action kicking off at the United States Grand Prix weekend in Austin, Texas on October 23.

Apple stated that Dolby Atmos will work together with "Dolby Vision to deliver a more immersive viewing experience," allowing "fans to be at the heart of the action and feel the speed, drama and emotion of Formula 1 at every moment."

The following is a statement from Oliver Schusser, Apple's Vice President of Apple Music and International Content, regarding today's announcement:

It is worth noting that Apple TV's current Formula 1 streaming rights remain limited to the United States market, and no additional payment is required beyond the Apple TV subscription.

Apple has previously made the Bahrain Grand Prix race content available for free streaming to US viewers, and has also partnered with Netflix to bring the eighth season of "Formula 1: Drive to Survive" to the Apple TV platform in the United States. Under the same partnership framework, the 2026 Canadian Grand Prix will also be broadcast simultaneously in the United States via Apple TV and Netflix.

Apple acquired Formula 1 streaming rights for the US market in 2025, as part of a five-year contract starting from the 2026 season, and has previously stated its intention to expand F1 race coverage to more regional markets.

Apple's broader partnership with Formula 1 also includes "F1: The Movie," which won the Academy Award for Best Sound earlier this year, and remains the highest-grossing theatrical release under Apple's banner to date.

Apple TV costs US$14.99 per month, or can be subscribed to through the Apple One bundle. The platform features many popular series and films, including "Ted Lasso," "Severance," "The Studio," "The Morning Show," "Shrinking," and "Silo."
